stem.text: A car is travelling at constant velocity. Its brakes are then applied, causing uniform deceleration.
Which graph shows the variation with distance $s$ of the velocity $v$ of the car?

A.alt: Graph with v on the vertical axis and s on the horizontal axis, both axes starting at 0. The curve is horizontal at first, then curves downward to zero at the end of the s axis.

B.alt: Graph with v on the vertical axis and s on the horizontal axis, both axes starting at 0. The line is horizontal at first, then falls in a straight line to zero on the s axis.

C.alt: Graph with v on the vertical axis and s on the horizontal axis, both axes starting at 0. The line is horizontal at first, then curves downward and levels off close to the s axis.

D.alt: Graph with v on the vertical axis and s on the horizontal axis, both axes starting at 0. The line is horizontal, then drops vertically to zero, and then continues along the s axis.
